result.title: Batched Contextual Reinforcement II: Does RLVR Need Long Rollout Windows?
result.summary: Long rollout windows make reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) expensive, yet simply shortening them can remove the correctness signal: when every single-problem rollout truncates before an answer, group-relative accuracy advantages vanish. As a technical continuation of Batched Contextual Reinforcement (BCR), we study how concurrent rewards relax this dependence on long windows. Concurrent Constraint Reinforcement (CCR) places three independently verifiable problems in one capped training completion. Correct answers completed before truncation retain credit, while a shared budget encourages shorter useful reasoning without an explicit length penalty. We connect this mechanism to conditional reward- and update-variance analyses and study 4B and 8B mathematical reasoning models. Against single-problem GRPO with a 32k window, CCR with an 8,000-token window reduces tokens per training step from 975,464 to 174,957 on 4B and from 793,832 to 165,788 on 8B, saving 82.1% and 79.1%, respectively. An 8B training trace shows increasing accuracy reward alongside shorter completions. Single-problem evaluations provide supporting evidence of retained reasoning quality. These results identify reward-preserving training structure as a practical route to lower per-step cost in short-window RLVR.

AI.brief_summary: 针对 RLVR 中长 rollout 窗口代价高、缩短窗口又会使组内相对优势信号消失的问题，提出 Concurrent Constraint Reinforcement：把三个可独立验证的数学题放入同一个有上限的 completion，截断前已完成的正确答案仍保留信用，共享预算促使推理更短，从而在 8k 窗口下大幅降低每步训练开销。
AI.relevance_reason: 纯文本 RLVR 训练效率工作，无视觉或多模态状态；但「截断仍保留信用 + 共享预算换取更短推理」这一训练结构，可能为 latent 或短轨迹推理训练中的贡献分配、长度与停止监督提供可核查线索，涉及奖励与更新方差的分析也可供参考。
